root_idea.summary: The root centers on the chin, the point where the lower jaws meet, and extends to actions, bodily descriptions, and shapes associated with it.
root_idea.development: From the anatomical base, the vocabulary develops meanings involving striking or resting on the chin, movement of the head, and figurative inclination or falling; related terms also describe the projecting throat region and an unevenly inclined bucket.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular citation form ذَقَنٌ; the supplied Quran form is its plural أَذْقَان.

senses.definition: The chin: the lower-jaw region where the two jaws meet.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic plural أَذْقَان occurs in expressions of falling or prostrating with the chins toward the ground; the construction may be rendered contextually as falling on one's face. It also occurs as the body part itself.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To strike the chin; also to strike a person on the rear neck or adjacent head with the inside of the hand, or to beat him with a stick.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form I verb with the person struck as its object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To place the chin on the hand, a staff, or a whip and lean upon it.
Of a bucket, to be or become large and inclined or uneven, of the type called ذَقُون or ذَقْنَاء.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the bucket’s shape or condition.
A Form III verb with the person straitened as its object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A decrepit, old and weak, or extremely aged man.
To seek support from a low, weak, or powerless person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A proverbial extension based on an overloaded camel using its chin to help itself rise.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In figurative expressions of trees or stones, to fall, bend down, or be overturned to the ground, expressed as falling to the chin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A metaphorical extension of the body-part expression to nonhuman objects.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The hair growing on the chin; the beard.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as vulgar or post-classical usage, and also as a Nabataean term.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel that lowers or relaxes her chin while walking, moves her head as she walks, or lengthens her stride with lively strength.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The descriptions vary in emphasis between chin movement, head movement, and brisk movement.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A leather bucket whose lip inclines to one side; a large or otherwise unevenly inclined bucket.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is also linked with the feminine form ذَقْنَاء in descriptions of an inclined bucket.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An anatomical region associated with the chin and upper throat or chest: the part beneath the chin, the throat’s projecting extremity, or an adjacent upper-chest region; it is also reported for the upper abdomen or stomach.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term has several attested anatomical applications, including the region reached by the chin and the area referred to in the expression “between my حَاقِنَة and my ذَاقِنَة.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man with a long chin; also one whose mouth is inclined or wry at the sides.
Applied figuratively to a woman whose pudendum is inclined or wry.
